title: Kevin Durant Claps Back After NBA's New Heave Rule Sparks Nikola Jokic Comparisons And European Bias Claims - NewsBreak
text:
By Kenny Nosay ,
1 hours ago
Kevin Durant (Image Credits: Imagn) Kevin Durant is the kind of ‘I’d die on that hill’ type of player. He’s unapologetic about hypothetical basketball debates and regularly engages with fans or the media on the popular social media platform X. However, like the rest of us, Durant isn’t always perfect with his opinions.
When ESPN Insider Shams Charania reported that the NBA will implement a new rule regarding end-of-period heaves for the 2025-26 season, nearly all players rejoiced—except Durant. Justin Termine, the host of NBA Today from SiriusXM NBA Radio, inexplicably called out the 15-time All-Star on X about the rule change. Rest assured, he was met with a swift response from the Houston Rockets forward, who’s always active on the platform.
“Durant can now go back to shooting heaves after not taking a single one since 2018 because he’s more concerned about his shooting % than helping his team win. Jokic, by the way, led the NBA with 22 last season in an example of someone who actually values winning over stats,” Justin Termine on X.
“We get it, we get it. You love European players over American born players….enjoy the heaves my boy, I probably still won’t take em,” Kevin Durant playfully replied.
Termine has a point in his take. Nuggets superstar Nikola Jokic is well-known for throwing heaves in end-of-quarter scenarios. While most don’t go in, others become highlights. Even the ridiculous, unsuccessful attempts Jokic had thrown out turned into a must-watch. Durant, on the other hand, doesn’t like those shot attempts. He rarely took any attempt beyond half-court during his career.
Can Kevin Durant Lead The Rockets To A Title? Kevin Durant (Image Credits: Imagn) After his unproductive two-year stint with the Phoenix Suns, Kevin Durant was traded to the Rockets this offseason. Seven teams were involved in the complicated trade, the largest in NBA history. He joins a Rockets team with many promising young players, such as Alperen Sengun and Amen Thompson. Sengun reached out to Durant after the trade and has welcomed him with open arms.
The Houston Rockets are one of the favorites to win a title next season. Most betting sites have them at the fifth spot in their odds of winning it all. Kevin Durant, who will turn 37 at the end of September, is still one of the best scorers in the league. If he can stay productive and injury-free, then the Rockets might make a run for the championship in 2026.
